title: F7 — the water surface, round 5. Round 4 failed at 2/10 with EVERY headline row measured at a threshold its own instrument shows to be unstable. This round finds a threshold that IS stable and says how it knows, removes ordinal drift from the instrument instead of measuring it, scores the water-hidden control nobody had scored, sweeps the band below 0.60 m at the pose that actually fails, shoots the motion five rounds have owed, and writes the reference item four critics have owed.
state: IN PROGRESS — written incrementally as runs land. Not final until `state` reads delivered-awaiting-critic.
verdict_this_answers: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-F7-WATER-r4.json (FAIL at 2/10, down from 3). biggest_gap GAP-W1-f7-shore-band-scaled-to-the-water-body-not-the-bank. Its ruling: KEEP the mechanism, set the default to 0.10 m, verify it at edge-b225 which nobody had swept below 0.60 m, report `presence` on every row, and run the mask control in BOTH orders.
what_i_could_not_do: **THE ACCEPTANCE FAILS ON BOTH HALVES AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT.** The r4 verdict's paired acceptance is `gradient_width_px >= 12` at the WORST pose of a complete 4-bearing Deep Marshes set AND `presence >= 90%` at EVERY pose in both regions. Measured at threshold 16 with an interleaved baseline: at `edge-b135` the shipped arm's presence is **51.38%**; at `edge-b225` the width is **1 px** and no band constant from 0.05 m to 1.20 m moves it. **Both clauses fail, at the pose that carries the positive result and at the pose that carries the negative one.** The change I shipped is a strict improvement on round 4 and it is not a pass, and a critic must not read the 32 px width at `edge-b135` as the round's headline.

**AND THE COST IS MOSTLY NOT THE CONSTANT I WAS SENT TO FIX, WHICH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS FILE.** At `edge-b135`, threshold 16: the depth colour with the shore alpha term switched off entirely (`no-shorefade`) reads **91.34%** presence; round 3's transmittance-gated fade with NO metre band (`r3`) reads **60.67%**; the shipped 0.10 m reads **51.38%**. So round 3's own fade costs ~30 points before round 4's constant costs its further ~9. **Fixing the constant was correct and it reaches about a quarter of the problem.** The remaining term is the `diffuseColor.a * 0.42` multiplier, which is round 3's and which nobody has been sent at. A sixth round that only tunes the band cannot clear a 90% presence bar.

**`TemporalVar` IS A HARD FAIL AND NOBODY HAD EVER MEASURED IT.** 0.000341 against a band of >= 0.002 and a hard-fail floor of 0.0005. I verified first that this is not HAZARDS §30's identity — all 30 temporal frames are distinct — and added the per-pixel control the spec's mean-based definition cannot see (water 0.000525, land 0.000107), which agrees. The land control's own `TemporalVar` is **0.000256**, i.e. static ground carries 75% as much temporal variance as our water. **With `FresnelDelta` and `ShoreDelta` already failing at their worst poses, `RI-VIS03` M12's 'any two failing = water is a blue plane hard fail' is now met three times over.** This is a worse position than round 4 reported, it is new information, and it is mine.

**THE ONE M12 SUB-METRIC F7 HAS BEEN PASSING CANNOT BE CLAIMED EITHER.** `NormalEnergy` reads 0.232–0.237 against a 0.035 band at every arm and every threshold — and `RI-VIS04` §8's supersample test, owed for four rounds and finally run, returns **64.95%** high-frequency survival on the shipped arm and 64.01% on round 2's. Under `RI-VIS11` §3 that is `unresolved`, and `unresolved` fails closed. So the high number is not evidence. Both arms read the same, so this is a standing property of our water and not something any recent round caused.

**THE S52 MATCHED-LUMINANCE NULL DID NOT RUN, AND THE REASON IS MY OWN MISTAKE.** I built the null as a sweep of constant-transmittance arms specifically to avoid round 4's bisection that never converged — and then invoked the `edge-b135` run with `--nulls 0.20,0.45` while passing an explicit `--arms` list that did not include them, so the null arms were defined and never captured. I noticed it reading my own output table, not before launching. A replacement run is queued behind the contention ceiling and may not land. **So, exactly as in round 4, no claim in this round is protected by a matched-luminance null, and my 0.10 m result is as unprotected as the build's was.** The one mitigation is that `no-shorefade` and `r3` are ablation arms rather than brightness controls and they do separate the terms — but they are not a null.

**THE WESTERN ROOTLANDS IS STILL 1 OF 4 BEARINGS AND I DID NOT RE-TAKE IT.** `RI-VIS03` M12a clause 1 requires >= 4 poses >= 90 degrees apart per region; round 4 had `edge-b225` only there and so does this round, because I spent the browser budget on the threshold question, the failing pose, the motion and the supersample test. **M12a clause 1 fails closed in the Western Rootlands for the second round running**, and the region matters more than its share of the evidence suggests: my own band census puts it at 100% band coverage at 1.20 m and 17.98% at 0.10 m, the largest change of any region, and round 4 measured its presence at 69.35%. It is unmeasured at the shipped value.

**I RAN BROWSERS WHILE `node tools/contention.mjs` REPORTED THE BOX OVER ITS CEILING, AND THE TOOL ASKS THAT THIS BE SAID.** Readings taken across this round: 2.70, 3.02, 3.13, 3.32, 3.33, 3.44, 3.81 (all GO) and **4.11, 4.47, 4.68, 4.80, 4.81 per core against a ceiling of 4.0 (all WAIT)**. I checked before every launch and launched only on a GO; the WAIT readings occurred while runs already in flight overlapped. **When the box went over I did not launch anything further and I did not kill a running measurement to make room** — the alternative was destroying banked-in-progress work, which HAZARDS §23 and §13 both argue against. The visible cost is that runs slowed to roughly 3–5 minutes per capture.

**I FOUND TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT WHILE IT WAS RUNNING, AND ONE OF THEM IS THE EXACT THING ROUND 4 WAS FAULTED FOR.** In both `--mode supersample` and `--mode motion` the per-arm `write()` fired BEFORE the results object was attached to the output, so a run killed by contention or by its own timeout would have left its numbers in a console log and not in the banked artifact — HAZARDS §18's shape, and precisely the criticism made of round 4's frame-time figures. I found it by opening the artifact instead of trusting the log, fixed both, and additionally moved `TemporalVar` into an offline tool that recomputes it from the banked PNGs, where it returns the identical 0.000341 from a separate code path. **The supersample run survived only because it happened to finish normally.**

**I DID NOT ABLATE THE CAUSE I NAMED FOR THE STIPPLE.** `RI-VIS11` establishes by measurement that the water's micro-detail is aliasing-class and not an ordered dither — the 4x4 phase signature is 0.28–0.61 LSB on water against 1.13–1.52 on the land the shader never touches. It then NAMES a candidate cause, the three procedural terms at 4.7 / 13.7 / 26.3 radians per world metre at `water.js:304-306`, and **I did not switch them off to prove it.** `ARBITRATION` S63's standing rule is that a mechanism may not be narrated unless the ablation was run, so the item states it as a candidate and sets `confidence: medium`. A future round should ablate the three terms individually.

**MY OWN NEW REFERENCE ITEM HAD A HOLE IN IT AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT FELL IN IT.** `RI-VIS11` §3's first draft banded `hf_survival >= 70%` and hard-failed `< 45%` and said nothing about the middle; the first number ever taken against it was 64.95%. I amended the item the same turn to make 45–70% `unresolved`, failing closed, per `ARBITRATION` S61. Its thresholds remain first-draft, derived from the physics of box-downsampling rather than from a corpus of measured reference plates, and the first build judged against them should be expected to argue with the exact numbers.

**AN UNEXPLAINED DISAGREEMENT BETWEEN MY OWN TWO WIDTH MEASURES.** At `edge-b135`, threshold 16, the closed-mask and raw widths agree on every arm (32/30, 31/29, 31/25) except `r3`, where closed reads **1** and raw reads **30**. That is on the arm that is supposed to have no band at all. The r4 critic attacked the closing and concluded it was the reliable half; here the anomaly is in the raw figure. I have no explanation, I did not choose between them, and both are reported on every row.

**NO BLIND PAIR, AGAIN, AND IT IS NOT MINE TO RUN.** `blind_status: not_possible`, 0, fail-closed. A builder cannot spawn a fresh judge; `CLAUDE.md` rule 0e puts it with the orchestrator. Question (2) the r4 build could not settle — *is a fade whose cost is a much darker starting region worth having at all* — is a look question, and the `presence` measure has now made the cost numeric without making it a judgement.

**NO FRAME-TIME READING AND I DID NOT ATTEMPT ONE.** Round 4 established with measurements that it is unobtainable on this box — 3703.09 ms/world-pass with a replicate spread of 5605.27 — and `game/src/engine.js` puts `renderCpuMs` in `_unmeasurable` in its own words because this container is SwiftShader. Repeating a measurement already shown to be unresolvable would have cost browser time the threshold question needed. Recorded as inherited-and-not-re-derived rather than as a result of mine.

**THE SMALL-BAND RANKING IS NOT RESOLVABLE AND I AM NOT PRETENDING IT IS.** The presence drift band at `edge-b225` is 96.09–100% over nine captures of the unchanged arm, so `band-0.30` (99.57%) and `band-0.60` (96.59%) sit inside it and are NOT distinguishable from an arm that changed nothing. My report tool flags them `~drift`. The b225 evidence supports 'the shipped 1.20 m costs real water' and supports no finer ordering than that. The choice of 0.10 m over 0.05 m or 0.20 m rests on the offline band census, not on the captures.

job_1_the_threshold_and_the_drift.the_finding_that_outranks_the_build: Round 4's every headline row is a threshold-6 row, and threshold 6's mask drifts +19.9% to +61.8% on an UNCHANGED arm. The r4 critic's remedy was to move to threshold 10. **Measured over a longer ordinal span than either round had, threshold 10 is NOT stable either** — see the table below. The stable threshold on this scene is **16**.
job_1_the_threshold_and_the_drift.how_this_round_measures_stability_differ: Rounds 3 and 4 took the pin twice, BACK TO BACK, and published that as the noise floor of a comparison spanning five to eight shader round-trips. HAZARDS §25a says in as many words that a replicate taken at a shorter interval than the comparison is not that comparison's noise floor. So this round re-captures the UNCHANGED baseline arm BEFORE AND AFTER EVERY ARM, and publishes the spread of the baseline's own repeated captures across the ordinals the arms actually occupy. That spread is printed beside every number by `tools/visual/f7-r5-report.mjs`.
job_1_the_threshold_and_the_drift.and_it_does_more_than_measure_the_drift_: Each arm is scored against the MEAN OF ITS TWO FLANKING BASELINES — one capture interval away on each side instead of eight — so monotonic drift cancels to first order by construction. This is HAZARDS §25a rule 1 in its strongest form: instead of putting one proven-identical null arm LAST to size the drift, the proven-identical null (`prefix` itself) is captured BETWEEN EVERY PAIR of arms and subtracted.

THE ANSWER, MEASURED — AND IT OVERTURNS.run: corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-F7-WATER-r5/dm-b225-sweep/ — NINE captures of the UNCHANGED baseline arm, interleaved through eight arms, i.e. spread across exactly the ordinals the comparison spans.
THE ANSWER, MEASURED — AND IT OVERTURNS.ruling: **THRESHOLD 10 IS NOT STABLE. THRESHOLD 16 IS.** The r4 critic wrote *'threshold 10 is the only stable threshold'* and set the round-5 acceptance at it. That conclusion rests on a PIN -> PIN2 back-to-back replicate, which measures drift over ONE capture interval. Measured over the interval the arms actually span, the same unchanged shader's own mask moves **33.68%** at threshold 10 and **0.26%** at threshold 16 — a 130x difference. **So I did not publish a threshold-10 headline row either.** Every headline number in this round is threshold 16, with the 0.26% band beside it.
THE ANSWER, MEASURED — AND IT OVERTURNS.and_the_ordinal_signature_is_visible_in_: At threshold 6 the arms' `own_mask_delta_pct` climbs 34.34 -> 52.95 -> 56.97 -> 58.23 -> 58.64 -> 58.80 -> 58.92 -> 59.05 in capture order, with the arm that changes the water LEAST (`no-shorefade`) reading the LARGEST value because it is captured last — HAZARDS §25a's exact signature, reproduced. At threshold 10 the same climb runs -0.51 -> 12.00 -> 24.51 -> 29.30 -> 31.12 -> 31.94 -> 32.33 -> 32.90. **At threshold 16 the same eight arms read -0.52, -0.52, -0.55, -0.51, -0.54, -0.69, -1.12, -0.27 — flat, no trend, no ordinal signature at all.**

the_drift_band_i_publish_beside_every_nu.gradient_width_px_closed: 0 px — the unchanged arm's width never moved

the_cleanest_comparison_is_ONE_UNCHANGED.ruling: **One unchanged arm, two capture positions: threshold 10 moves by 12.52 points and threshold 16 moves by 0.02 points.** HAZARDS §25a rule 2 says that if an ordering reverses with the sequence it is ordinal rather than the arm. It does, at thresholds 6 and 10, and it does not at 16. **The §25a confound is confirmed independently, and threshold 16 is confirmed order-independent as well as ordinal-independent.**

THE ORDER-REVERSED CONTROL — HAZARDS §25.and_a_free_identity_check_fell_out_of_it: Because the change shipped between runs, `fixed` in the reverse run IS the 0.10 m configuration. It reads **presence 100.16%** where the explicitly-set `band-0.10` arm in the same run reads **100.37%** — the same configuration reached by two different routes (source default vs uniform override), captured at different ordinals, agreeing to **0.21 percentage points**. That confirms the shipped default is what I say it is and that the arm machinery is not vacuous.
THE ORDER-REVERSED CONTROL — HAZARDS §25.AND_IT_GIVES_THE_CLEANEST_BEFORE_AND_AFT: `fixed` means 'the source default', so the forward run measured it at 1.20 m and the reverse run — launched after the change landed — measured it at 0.10 m. **Same arm name, same pose (`edge-b225`), same threshold (16), same tool, same site and seed: presence 83.35% -> 100.16%.** That is +16.81 percentage points of the baseline's visible water, bought by one constant, at the pose round 4 failed hardest on. It is also the round's tidiest reversal proof: the two rows differ by one number in one file.
THE ORDER-REVERSED CONTROL — HAZARDS §25.reading: At `edge-b225` the shipped 0.10 m is indistinguishable from having no band at all (100.16 / 100.37 / 100.40, all inside a 96.4–100% drift band). **It costs nothing at this pose and buys nothing at this pose** — which is the correct behaviour for a shore band at a pose whose water is too deep for it to act on, and is exactly what the offline census predicted from the field.
THE ORDER-REVERSED CONTROL — HAZARDS §25.and_the_baseline_reproduced_ACROSS_PROCE: The reverse run's baseline captures read 68.623 / 67.740 / 67.277 at threshold 6 — **identical to the forward run's first three baseline captures to three decimal places**, in a separate process, a separate browser and a later commit. The instrument is reproducible; it is the threshold choice that was not.

A_LIMIT_ON_MY_OWN_HEADLINE_THAT_I_FOUND_.the_finding: **Stabilising the MASK does not stabilise the WIDTH.** At `edge-b045` the unchanged baseline arm reads `gradient_width_px` = **20 at threshold 10** and **1 at threshold 16** — a 20x difference from a six-level threshold change, while the two masks differ by only **2.4%** (251,825 vs 245,818 px).
A_LIMIT_ON_MY_OWN_HEADLINE_THAT_I_FOUND_.and_neither_reading_is_degenerate: I checked rather than assuming: both carry a real measurement with no `reason` field, and spans of 16.82 and 10.60 luma levels against the instrument's 0.6 minimum. The mechanism is visible in the anchors — the tighter threshold-16 mask excludes the darkest near-shore pixels, so the near anchor rises from 58.85 to 63.74 and the profile's 10–90% crossing collapses.
A_LIMIT_ON_MY_OWN_HEADLINE_THAT_I_FOUND_.what_it_costs_this_round: My threshold-16 headline is well founded **for `presence` and for the mask**, which is what I measured stability on and what the drift bands cover. It is **NOT** established that `gradient_width_px` is stable at threshold 16 — at `edge-b135` the two thresholds agree (32 vs 34) and at `edge-b225` they agree (1 vs 2), but at `edge-b045` they disagree by 20x. **So the width figures in this round should be read as threshold-conditional and the `>= 12 px` acceptance clause is being evaluated on a quantity that is not yet shown to be stable at any threshold.** Round 4 was failed partly for exactly this and I am not going to claim I have fixed it when I have only fixed it for the mask.
A_LIMIT_ON_MY_OWN_HEADLINE_THAT_I_FOUND_.what_would_settle_it: The same per-threshold drift measurement I ran for the mask, run for the width, across a pose set rather than one pose — i.e. capture the unchanged baseline arm N times at every declared bearing and publish the width spread per threshold per pose. That is one run of baselines only, no arms, and it is cheap. I did not have the budget.

job_1_the_threshold_and_the_drift.and_it_corrects_my_own_brief_which_the_r: My brief relayed that HAZARDS §25 is *not* measured by round 4 because `own_mask_delta_pct` tracks capture ordinal, and that the +23.24% quoted as proof of the per-arm mask hazard is an ordinal artefact. **CONFIRMED and extended: I reproduce the ordinal climb at thresholds 6 and 10 in a fresh run with a different arm list, and I show it DISAPPEARS at threshold 16.** So the confound is not merely ordinal — it is ordinal *at unstable thresholds*, and choosing a stable threshold removes it without any ordering trick. §25's rule (pin the mask) is untouched and this round still pins it.

job_2_the_failing_pose_swept_below_0.60_.what_nobody_had_done: The r4 build swept 0.60 / 1.20 / 1.35 at `edge-b225` and concluded 'no band constant rescues it, therefore it is not a tuning problem'. The build's failing pose is edge-b225, where I did NOT test below 0.60. Nobody should read "0.10 m rescues edge-b225" into that table.'* **This round ran it.**

TWO_FINDINGS_AND_THEY_POINT_OPPOSITE_WAY.1_the_r4_BUILD_was_right_about_this_pose: **No band constant rescues `edge-b225`.** Swept across a 24x range from 0.05 m to 1.20 m, the waterline width is 1 px at threshold 16 and never exceeds the baseline's own 2 px at threshold 10. The width at this pose is a property of the scene, not of the shader, and I am reporting that even though it is the half that does not flatter the change I shipped.
TWO_FINDINGS_AND_THEY_POINT_OPPOSITE_WAY.2_the_r4_CRITIC_was_right_that_1.20_m_is: **At the same pose, 0.10 m returns 17.0 percentage points of presence over 1.20 m (100.35% vs 83.35%) for identical width.** That is the whole ruling, now measured at the pose that actually fails rather than inferred from the pose that does not. `presence` falls monotonically with the band constant across all seven arms — 100.4, 100.4, 100.3, 100.1, 99.6, 96.6, 83.3 — while width never moves. A constant that buys nothing and costs seventeen points is dominated.
TWO_FINDINGS_AND_THEY_POINT_OPPOSITE_WAY.and_it_cross_validates_the_r4_critic: My interleaved `fixed` reads 83.3% where the r4 critic's drift-carrying protocol read 82.3% at the same pose. About one point apart, in the direction drift correction predicts.

and_it_falsifies_the_name_everybody_has_.the_test: An ordered dither is a FIXED function of screen position, so every pixel sharing an (x mod 4, y mod 4) phase gets the same offset. Bucket the masked pixels by that phase and the sixteen means separate systematically under a dither and agree under anything else. Also the 2x2 parity contrast.
and_it_falsifies_the_name_everybody_has_.ruling: **The phase signature is under two thirds of an 8-bit level on water and is two to five times LARGER on the land the water shader never touches. There is no ordered dither on our water.** Four verdicts have now inherited that diagnosis from each other. This is ARBITRATION S63's family — a mechanism stated once and travelling as established because nobody ran the ablation.

what_IS_there_and_it_is_real.reading: The water ADDS ~50% more pixel-to-pixel energy than the same pixels carry with the water hidden, so the energy is the shader's. And the water's ratio sits at ~0.92 where land's is ~0.73 — on a resolved surface the difference between two pixels GROWS with separation, so water's energy is concentrated at the finest scale the pixel grid can carry. **That is the signature of a signal sampled past its Nyquist limit.** The candidate cause is in F7's own source and is not a mystery: `water.js:304-306` adds procedural terms at 4.7, 13.7 and 26.3 radians per world metre with no mip chain, no derivative filtering and no distance rolloff.
what_IS_there_and_it_is_real.what_i_did_NOT_establish: That those three terms ARE the cause. I have shown the defect is aliasing-class rather than dithering-class and named a candidate; I have not ablated the three terms. RI-VIS11 says so in its own provenance note and sets `confidence: medium`.
what_IS_there_and_it_is_real.and_it_is_visible: In the orbit frames the same dotted patterning is plainly on the TREES and the bank as much as on the water, which is what a screen-wide sampling artefact looks like and is not what a water-shader dither would look like.

the_ruling_i_made_and_what_would_overtur.ruling: **KEEP the mechanism. SHIP 0.10 m. I am NOT claiming F7 and I am NOT claiming the acceptance — it fails on both halves.**
why_ship_0.10_rather_than_keep_1.20: It is DOMINATED, measured twice in my own instrument at the threshold I have shown to be stable. The width is a step function of whether a band exists, not of its size — 1 px at `r3`, 32 px at 0.10 m, and no further gain out to 1.20 m. So the larger constant buys nothing but absence.
the_ruling_i_made_and_what_would_overtur.why_not_revert_the_mechanism_entirely_to: Because `RI-VIS04` §9's MIN BAR names a shoreline depth fade as a required component, and this term is the only thing in the shader that produces a waterline at all: without it the width is 1 px. Reverting would trade a measured 32 px softening for a measured 1 px step and put the MIN BAR component back to absent. **But a critic could reasonably rule the other way and I want the numbers for that ruling on the record, not buried:** at `edge-b135` the fade costs 48.6 points of presence to buy that width (100% -> 51.38%), and a reviewer who weights 'the starting region's water is half invisible' above 'the waterline is soft' should revert. I considered it and did not do it, because the cost is now attributable and the term that carries it is NOT the one I was sent to fix.

MY_RULING_ON_THE_QUESTION_THE_NUMBERS_AC.the_question: Round 5 was sent at the band constant. The decomposition says the band constant is about a quarter of the cost. So what should round 6 attack?
MY_RULING_ON_THE_QUESTION_THE_NUMBERS_AC.the_evidence: At `edge-b135`, threshold 16: `no-shorefade` (shore alpha term entirely off) 91.34% · `r3` (transmittance fade, no metre band) 60.67% · `band-0.10` (shipped) 51.38% · `fixed` 1.20 m 41.99%. **The single line doing the damage is `diffuseColor.a = mix(diffuseColor.a, diffuseColor.a * .42, esShoreT)` at `water.js`. Wherever `esShoreT` saturates, the water's alpha is multiplied by 0.42 — and that multiplier is ROUND 3's, not round 4's, and no round has ever been sent at it.**
MY_RULING_ON_THE_QUESTION_THE_NUMBERS_AC.my_ruling: **Round 6 should attack the 0.42 alpha multiplier, not the band constant.** The band is now correctly scaled and further tuning of it is inside the drift band. A sweep of the multiplier — 0.42 / 0.60 / 0.75 / 0.85 — at `edge-b135` and `edge-b225`, scored on `presence` and `gradient_width_px` at threshold 16, is one uniform and one run, and it is the only lever left that is large enough to move `presence` from 51% toward the 90% the acceptance asks for.
MY_RULING_ON_THE_QUESTION_THE_NUMBERS_AC.what_would_overturn_it: If the softening width collapses as the multiplier rises — i.e. if the waterline is only visible BECAUSE the water goes 58% transparent there — then the two cannot be separated by this constant and the remedy is a genuine depth-buffer fade (`RI-VIS04` §9's HAVE names a depth-buffer read, which needs a depth prepass in `renderer.js`, a file F7 does not own). **That is a one-run falsification and I did not have the browser budget to run it**, so this ruling is a recommendation with its own test attached, not a finding.

what_would_make_this_status_wrong: **If `gradient_width_px` is not stable at threshold 16 either.** I proved mask stability and then reported widths, and at `edge-b045` the unchanged arm's width is 20 at threshold 10 and 1 at threshold 16. I flagged it rather than burying it, but a critic could reasonably rule that every width row in this round — including my 32 px — is unreadable until the width's own per-threshold drift is measured across the pose set. That is the attack I would make.

**If the S52 null would have reproduced the 32 px width.** It did not run. A constant-transmittance arm at matched luminance that produces a 32 px 'waterline' would void my headline in both directions, and I have no evidence either way.

**If the interleaved flanking baseline is itself wrong.** It assumes drift is approximately linear over one capture interval on each side. If drift is stepwise — e.g. a reflection target refreshing every N frames — the mean of two flanking captures is not the right correction and my presence figures carry a bias I have not characterised.

**If `presence` is the wrong measure of 'is there water'.** It is a luma ratio against a water-hidden frame, so a change that made the water the same brightness as the bed but visibly wrong would score 100%. It measures how much the water changes the picture, not whether it looks like water.

**If my choice of 0.10 m over 0.05 m or 0.20 m matters.** It rests on the offline band census, not on the captures, because all three sit inside the presence drift band at `edge-b225`. If the census's radius or its 1.35 m clamp is the wrong population, the choice is arbitrary within that range.

**If RI-VIS11's `unresolved` band lets a real defect through.** I wrote the item and then wrote its middle band after my own first measurement fell in the gap. A bar amended to accommodate the first number taken against it deserves suspicion, which is why I made the middle fail closed rather than pass.
self_audit.did_i_grade_my_own_work: No. I have recorded that the acceptance fails on both halves at the shipped value, that `TemporalVar` is a newly-measured HARD FAIL that makes M12's two-or-more clause met three times over, that the sub-metric F7 has been passing is `unresolved` under a bar I wrote this turn, that the S52 null did not run because of my own invocation error, that the Western Rootlands is still 1 of 4 bearings, and that the width measure I report is not shown to be stable. A critic decides.
self_audit.numbers_i_inherited_rather_than_derived: In the measurement sections, none — every figure came from a file I opened or a run I launched this turn, and where I re-derived one of the r4 critic's I say so and give both. THREE EXPLICIT EXCEPTIONS, all labelled in place: (1) round 4's frame-time figures, quoted only as round 4's and not re-run; (2) round 4's `depthWrite`/transparency-sort result, quoted only as round 4's and not re-run; (3) round 4's worst-pose `FresnelDelta` (0.03085) and `ShoreDelta` (0.00610), which I cite when saying M12's two-or-more clause is met — those are the r4 critic's numbers at threshold 6, I did not re-derive them at threshold 16, and my `TemporalVar` hard fail stands on its own regardless.
